solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: That can be published after undoing triple ban

indicators.note: undoing the words triple ban loosens their letters so they can be put back together differently

explanation.surface: Something becomes fit to print once a threefold prohibition is lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Material that is fit or suitable to appear in print is, by definition, publishable.

clue.text: Appear suddenly with report before judge

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, a pop
to be up before a judge is to appear in court

explanation.surface: Someone comes in with a statement to put in front of a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop up is to emerge or show yourself unexpectedly.

clue.text: Detaining a shady criminal for now

indicators.note: criminal suggests the words detaining a shady are wrongly arranged, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Police holding a dodgy lawbreaker, for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase refers to the present time, nowadays.

clue.text: Clutching honour, weary and full of beams?

indicators.note: clutching shows the weary word holding the honour inside it

parts.note: weary means tired
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone tired, gripping an award, beams with happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of beams' suggests smiling; it means made of wooden beams.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbered house is built with wooden joists and frames, so it has many beams.

clue.text: Defender has boot out for rebound

parts.note: a back is a defender in football or rugby
to boot someone out of a job is to fire them

explanation.surface: A footballer's kick goes out and bounces back.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that backfires rebounds on the person who made it.

clue.text: Drink for one lifting medal

parts.note: EG (for example) means for one

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue sends the medal word upward, so it is read from the bottom

parts.note: a gong is slang for a medal

explanation.surface: An athlete holds a medal aloft and is rewarded with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a creamy beverage of eggs, milk and often spirits, drunk at Christmas.

clue.text: Firm punch nails cheating brother

indicators.note: a punch that nails something holds it fast, so the firm is gripped inside the punch

parts.note: a jab is a quick punch
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company's blow strikes home against a sibling who cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Jacob tricks his twin Esau out of his birthright and their father's blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Jacob is the classic deceitful sibling, swindling his elder twin Esau.

clue.text: Mexican city university involved in conflict — centre for rendezvous

indicators.note: involved in places the university letter inside the conflict word

parts.note: a jar is a clash or quarrel

indicators.note: centre for takes the two middle letters of the word rendezvous

parts.note: middle two letters of rendezvous

explanation.surface: A university is caught up in a dispute at the heart of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciudad Juarez is a large border city in Mexico, opposite El Paso, Texas.

clue.text: Gardener with top rating, one landed gentry ultimately toast

parts.note: to cap is to top
an AB (able seaman) is a naval rating
I is the Roman numeral one
lit means landed, as a bird lit on a branch

indicators.note: ultimately takes only the final letter of the word gentry

parts.note: last letter of gentry
to toast bread is to brown it

explanation.surface: A top-rated gardener, one of the landed gentry, ends up done for.
explanation.walkthrough: Capability Brown was an 18th-century English landscape gardener. 'Landed gentry' looks like one phrase; it splits into LIT and the last letter of gentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot Brown designed the parks of many English country houses, the most famous landscape gardener.

clue.text: Broadcaster's raised promotion after he's become materialist

indicators.note: after places the promotion piece behind he
a broadcaster speaks over the air, so the word for raised is heard rather than read

parts.note: children who are raised are bred
he, the 's being a link
an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: A promotion goes to someone's head and turns them greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, so a breadhead is someone obsessed with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadhead is a slang term for a person mainly interested in making money.

clue.text: US runner returned old cap and waterproof

indicators.note: returned means the pieces for old and cap are read back the other way

parts.note: to top something is to cap it
a mac (mackintosh) is a waterproof coat

explanation.surface: An American athlete handed back a vintage hat and a raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: A runner in crosswords is often a river; the Potomac flows through Washington DC.
explanation.definitionFit: A river runs, so the crossword calls it a runner; this one is a major American river.

clue.text: Hook right in front of gas cooker?

indicators.note: front of picks out only the opening letter of the word gas

parts.note: first letter of gas
a cooker is a cooking apple, one grown for cooking rather than eating raw

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a hook on the right in front of a gas stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas cooker' looks like one kitchen appliance; it splits, with gas giving its first letter and cooker standing for a cooking apple.
explanation.definitionFit: To hook something is to seize or grip it, which is what grappling does.

clue.text: Maybe "medal's" sounding like "meddles"

indicators.note: sounding like tells us the answer is said the same way as a synonym of meddles

parts.note: someone who pries meddles in others' business

explanation.surface: A grammar note: the word medal's is pronounced just like meddles.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue pretends to be a remark about two words that sound alike; in fact a medal is an example of the answer, and the homophone is of a synonym of meddles, not of meddles itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is one example of an award, which is why the clue hedges with Maybe.

clue.text: Few bolder twists in the plot of The Black Tulip?

definitions.text: the plot of The Black Tulip?

indicators.note: twists works the letters of few bolder round into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A novel's storyline has fewer daring turns than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Tulip is a novel by Dumas, so 'plot' looks like its storyline; here it is a garden plot where a tulip grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip of any colour grows in a garden bed, which is the plot it belongs to.

clue.text: Good, nowadays, to obtain line in fashionable devices?

parts.note: AD (anno domini) labels the present era
to get is to obtain
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: These days it is good to acquire the latest range of trendy gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers gizmos collectively, especially trendy modern ones, hence the question mark on fashionable.

clue.text: Its community spirit all that remains?

definitions.text: Its community spirit all that remains?

parts.words: Its community spirit all that remains?
parts.note: community spirit is read literally: the only inhabitants left are spirits, as in a deserted settlement

explanation.walkthrough: 'Community spirit' normally means neighbourly feeling; here it means the phantoms of a place everyone has left.
explanation.definitionFit: An abandoned settlement, emptied of people, is said to be haunted only by its past.

clue.text: Head off for shelter?

indicators.note: the head of the word for is its first letter, so only that letter is used

parts.note: first letter of for
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Someone makes a dash for cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: to head off for shelter is to run away, and the head of for plus shelter builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: To head off is to leave quickly, the same as running away from danger.

clue.text: Look back on motorway with a glower

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
M is the abbreviation for motorway (M1)
an ember glows, so it is a glower

explanation.surface: A driver on the motorway glances in the mirror with a scowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' looks like a scowl; read as glow-er, it is something that glows.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall the past is to look back in memory.

clue.text: Fairy tale ending for Viktoria Plzen: United run ragged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: ending for takes the last letter of Viktoria

parts.note: last letter of Viktoria

indicators.note: run ragged means the letters are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A football report: Viktoria Plzen's season has a happy ending after they run United ragged.
explanation.walkthrough: Viktoria Plzen is a Czech football club. R for run and the last letter of Viktoria lead, and 'ragged' rearranges PLZEN with U to give PUNZEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapunzel is the Grimm brothers' story of the girl with very long hair locked in a tower.

clue.text: Just by lake has left stone

indicators.note: has left says the lake has gone out of the word for just

parts.note: only means just, as in just one
X is the multiplication sign, read as by (three by four)

explanation.surface: A rock sits right beside a lake that someone has walked away from.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Occupied half-forgotten, antediluvian houses

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ancient dwellings, half-remembered, from before the Flood were lived in.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that has tenants living in it is lived in, so it is not vacant.

clue.text: Buying church benefits my son, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect, used of the words my son I, marks them as doubtful and needing rearrangement

explanation.surface: A parent suspects their son is profiting from the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony, named after Simon Magus, is the sin of paying for clerical office or sacraments.

clue.text: Areas containing unknown meadow plant

indicators.note: containing shows the two area letters holding the unknown between them

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, and two of them, AA, make areas
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y
a lea is a meadow

explanation.surface: Fields that hold an unidentified meadow flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An azalea is a flowering shrub of the rhododendron family.

clue.text: Flap that is holding in large crate

indicators.note: holding means the flap word grips the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a tizz is a state of agitation, a flap
taken as written
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Panic, apparently, contained inside a big packing case.
explanation.walkthrough: A crate is slang for an old, rickety car; the Tin Lizzie was the nickname of the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is informal for a battered old car, and the Model T Ford was nicknamed that.

clue.text: Feeling less in need of new pigment

indicators.note: in need of means the word lacks the letter for new, so it is taken away

parts.note: something number (more numb) has less feeling

explanation.surface: An emotional state with less feeling that badly wants something fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: Number here is not the counting word but numb with -er, more numb.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural brown earth used as a colouring for paint.

clue.text: Firefly, maybe, with silky coat from South America

indicators.note: in a down clue, from South means reading upward, so the coat word is reversed

parts.note: fur is an animal's soft coat
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: An insect with a silky coat comes from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Firefly is not the insect: Rufus T. Firefly is the Groucho Marx character in Duck Soup, so Firefly is an example of someone with this first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The film character's first name is Rufus, hence the 'maybe' signalling an example.

clue.text: Being continually lucky registered somewhere?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: enjoying a run of successes
second meaning: written on a list or register, a roll

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is read literally: someone entered on a register is on a roll.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a winning streak, while literally it means listed on a roster.

clue.text: Kick-start on your bike

parts.note: a buzz is a kick, a thrill
the off is the start of a race

explanation.surface: Someone tells a motorcyclist to kick-start the engine and get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your bike' is British slang for 'go away', and the kick-start sounds like part of the motorbike picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are rude British ways of telling someone to leave.

clue.text: Poor tips from men we maybe trusted implicitly

indicators.note: tips are the end points, so the closing letter of each of the next five words is taken

explanation.surface: Men we perhaps relied on without question gave poor advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy people are those lacking money, the same as poor.

clue.text: Craft excellent courses on plain English speaking

indicators.note: on means the courses come after the speech piece in the answer

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI
RP, Received Pronunciation, is standard English speech
lanes are the courses marked out in a pool or on a track

explanation.surface: A boat or plane moves along excellent channels over flat land with English being spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain English speaking is not a homophone signal; it is RP, Received Pronunciation, the standard accent of British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft are craft, and the American spelling of aeroplanes is used here.
